# Lens: stockouts-unconstrained — inventory_stockouts.csv and unconstrained demand

**Headline.** `inventory_stockouts.csv` is formally clean (5,830 rows, 0 duplicates, 0 label/date variants, 0 impossible values) and is generated by an exact arithmetic machine that we have fully reverse-engineered: `Shipped = floor(fill x (Requested + Carried_In))`, `Backordered = floor(0.4 x shortfall)` for the four operational reasons and `0` for "Semiconductor allocation", `Lost = shortfall - Backordered`, `Carried_In(t) = Backordered(t-1)` (3,108 / 3,108 consecutive pairs), `Stockout_Days = round(30 x (1 - fill))`; all hold in 100% of rows, while the documented identity `Fill_Rate_Pct = Shipped / (Requested + Carried_In)` holds in only 2.3% of rows because `Fill_Rate_Pct` is the latent allocation fraction, not the realised ratio. After cleaning, train `Units_Sold` equals `Shipped_Units` exactly in every exactly-recoverable error class (5,767 / 5,804 matched rows; the 37 exceptions are 36 India "pack-of-10" rounding losses and 1 blank row), so the file is also a ground-truth validator for the cleaning rules. The month after a back-ordered stockout ships `own demand + Backordered(t)` exactly, even when that month is not in the file (141 of 1,048 such months are pure "phantom orders" in zero-demand months). The file is incomplete in two different ways: (i) the semiconductor shortage hits **every** Electrical Assemblies (ELA) series-month from 2021-03 to 2022-09, but only 69.1% of those cells are listed (1,925 unlisted cells, fill following a deterministic depth curve times a per-series severity, imputable with 5.3% WAPE and -0.2% bias); (ii) operational stockouts are iid random events (about 0.8% of series-months, uniform over time, family, region, channel and demand level), about 79% listed, so about 413 (95% CI 328-516) are hidden, of which 105 are recoverable with arithmetic certainty and the rest are statistically undetectable at useful precision. Unconstrained demand exceeds shipments by 0.91% overall but by +44.8% for ELA in 2021 and +29.2% in 2022; total lost sales are about 112k units / about USD 114M, of which the ELA shortage alone is 78,347 units (about 70%) and USD 88.4M (about 78%).

All numbers below were computed with the scripts in `research/scratch/stockouts-unconstrained/` on my own working clean of train (rough-clean parquet + the unit fixes validated in Finding 3). Totals may move by a few units when the official cleaning pipeline replaces it.

---

## 1. The stockout file is formally clean; the only "mess" is semantic

**(a) Evidence**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Rows / columns | 5,830 / 11 |
| Date format | 100% `YYYY-MM`, 94 distinct months (2019-01 .. 2026-10) |
| SKU_ID format | 100% `AAA-999`, 520 SKUs |
| Region labels | exactly the 6 canonical labels, no variants, no whitespace |
| Reason labels | 5 canonical values: Semiconductor allocation 4,314; Logistics delay 391; Supplier quality hold 381; Capacity constraint 377; Tooling breakdown 367 |
| Blank cells | 0 in every column |
| Exact duplicate rows / duplicate (Date, SKU, Region) keys | 0 / 0 |
| Negative values, Shipped > Requested + Carried_In, Lost < 0, Fill > 100 | 0 |
| Fill range / Stockout_Days range | 15.0 .. 98.0 / 1 .. 25 |
| Rows for SKUs absent from master, before launch, after EOL, outside the series' active span in train, MEA before 2022-01 | 0 |
| Rows with `Requested_Units = 0` | 870 (14.9%); 825 of them are all-zero rows (Requested = Carried_In = Shipped = Backordered = Lost = 0) that still carry a Fill_Rate_Pct, Stockout_Days and Reason; 45 have only carried-in units |

The 14.9% zero-request share equals the natural zero-demand share of train (14.76% of unlisted cells): the generator draws the stockout flag independently of demand, so a "stockout" can fall on a month with no order.

**(b) Classification:** generator_structure. **(c) Confidence:** high.

**(d) Rule.** Load the file as is (no label/date repair needed). Keep the 825 all-zero rows as flags only (no demand correction, zero lost units). Data-quality report line: "inventory_stockouts.csv: 0 format issues, 825 no-impact rows, 1 documentation conflict (Fill_Rate_Pct, Finding 2), known incompleteness quantified in Findings 5-6".

## 2. Exact accounting identities (the generator's supply block)

**(a) Evidence**

| Identity | Holds in |
|---|---|
| `Lost = Requested + Carried_In - Shipped - Backordered` | 5,830 / 5,830 (100%) |
| `Carried_In(t) = Backordered(t-1)` when month t-1 of the same series is listed | 3,108 / 3,108 (100%) |
| `Shipped = floor(fill_latent x (Requested + Carried_In))` with `fill_latent` anywhere inside the 0.1-point rounding interval of `Fill_Rate_Pct` | 5,005 / 5,005 rows with a positive denominator (100%); `round()` instead of `floor()` is feasible in only 52.1% |
| Documented `Fill_Rate_Pct = 100 x Shipped / (Requested + Carried_In)` | equal at 1 decimal in only 2.3% of rows; differs by more than 1 point in 58.8%; maximum difference 93.4 points; the 825 zero-denominator rows still have a fill value |
| `Stockout_Days = round(30 x (1 - fill))` | 5,771 / 5,830 with the printed fill (99.0%); 100% feasible with the latent fill inside its rounding interval |
| `Backordered = floor(0.4 x shortfall)` for the 4 operational reasons | 1,516 / 1,516 (100%) |
| `Backordered = 0` (whole shortfall lost) for Semiconductor allocation | 4,314 / 4,314 (100%) |
| Operational fill distribution | Uniform(15, 70): deciles 15.0, 21.2, 26.2, 31.9, 37.3, 43.2, 48.6, 53.7, 59.2, 64.6, 70.0; KS p = 0.48; mean 42.8; identical for all 4 reasons; no correlation between consecutive months (r = -0.004) |

File totals: Requested 235,319; Carried_In 3,948; Shipped 140,554; Backordered 16,886; Lost 81,827. Operational rows: Requested 72,146, Shipped 32,458, Backordered 16,886, Lost 26,690. Semiconductor rows: Requested 163,173, Shipped 108,096, Lost 55,137.

**(b) Classification:** generator_structure; the Fill_Rate_Pct definition is a reference_conflict (documentation vs data). **(c) Confidence:** high.

**(d) Rule.** Treat `Fill_Rate_Pct` as the latent allocation fraction. For the dashboard show a realised fill `Shipped / (Requested + Carried_In)` computed by us, and log the documentation conflict in the data-quality report. Use the identities as unit tests on the loaded file (all must be 100%).

## 3. Train `Units_Sold` equals `Shipped_Units` exactly once train errors are fixed; the file is ground truth for the cleaning rules

**(a) Evidence.** Raw comparison (rough-clean train, join on Date-SKU-Region): 5,789 of 5,830 stockout rows find a train row; 5,637 of them (97.4%) are exactly equal. The 193 others, by cause:

| Disagreement class (train side) | Stockout rows | Fix | Fixed value equals Shipped |
|---|---|---|---|
| No train row at all (true missing row inside the series' active span) | 26 | take Shipped from the stockout file | n/a (recovered) |
| Train row had a blank Region (found by elimination: the one region of that SKU with no row that month, tie broken by customer) | 15 | region fill | 15 / 15 |
| Units blank, price > 0, revenue present | 70 | units = revenue / price | 70 / 70 |
| Units blank or "-" with price = 0 and revenue = 0 | 19 | units = 0 | 19 / 19 |
| Units blank, revenue blank (LatAm ERP-migration months) | 1 | not recoverable from train (THM-033, Latin America, 2023-04: Shipped 65, Requested 102) | recovered from file |
| Negative units | 14 | absolute value | 14 / 14 |
| Units x 100 (revenue / (units x price) = 0.01, price normal) | 4 | divide by 100 | 4 / 4 |
| Units x 10 (ratio 0.1, price normal) | 2 | divide by 10 | 2 / 2 |
| India 2021-07..12 "pack of 10": price x 10 and units = round-half-up(true / 10) | 42 | x 10 is only approximate | 6 / 42 exact; rule `units_raw = max(1, round(Shipped/10))` matches 42 / 42 |

Classes where the units were right and only price or revenue was wrong, all confirmed by Shipped: price x 100 (11 / 11), price in EUR at 0.89 (48 / 48, Europe 2022), revenue x 10 (9 / 9), other revenue mismatch (3 / 3), positive units with price and revenue 0 (10 / 10). Rows with no error: 5,571 / 5,571 equal.

After fixes: 5,767 of 5,804 matched rows equal (99.4%), and 100% in every class that is exactly recoverable. Train therefore records constrained shipments, never requests.

Examples: CEL row for ELA-008 / North America / 2021-05 shows -107 (Shipped 107); ELA-067 / Europe / 2021-06 shows 900 with revenue 11,443.14 = 9 x 1,271.46 (Shipped 9); ELA-014 / India / 2021-07 shows 2 units at 5,788.90 (list price 578.89; Shipped 18).

**(b) Classification:** data_error (each class) plus generator_structure (train = shipped). **(c) Confidence:** high.

**(d) Rule.** (1) In the cleaning pipeline, after de-duplication, overlay `Units_Sold := Shipped_Units` for every listed cell: this repairs 26 missing rows, 1 unrecoverable blank and 36 India pack-of-10 cells exactly (list in `train_cells_recoverable_from_stockout_file.csv`). (2) Add a pipeline test "cleaned Units_Sold == Shipped_Units on listed cells, by error class" using `train_vs_shipped_validation.csv` as the expected table. (3) For the 343 unlisted India pack-of-10 rows (385 in total, India only, 2021-07..12, about 78 SKUs) use `units x 10` and mark +/-5 units of rounding uncertainty.

## 4. Back-order dynamics: next month's sales contain the back-ordered units, exactly

**(a) Evidence.** 1,321 listed rows have `Backordered > 0`. In 251 the next month is also listed and its `Carried_In` equals that back-order (Finding 2). In 1,054 the next month is inside the history and **not** listed (the remaining 16 are 2026-10 rows whose next month is the first forecast month); 1,048 of those have a usable train value:

| Test on `Units_Sold(t+1) - Backordered(t)` | Count |
|---|---|
| exactly 0 (the month's own demand is zero, the only units are the catch-up) | 141 (13.45%; natural zero share 14.76%) |
| `Units_Sold(t+1) = 0` | 1 (expected about 155 if the carry did not exist) |
| negative (shipped less than the carried-in units) | 14, each a hidden second-month stockout (Finding 6) |
| control: listed operational rows with zero back-order, next month unlisted | 16.1% have `Units_Sold(t+1) = 0` (n = 155) |

So `Units_Sold(t+1) = own demand(t+1) + Backordered(t)` whether or not month t+1 is listed. After removing the carry, the 1,034 corrected months sit at 0.956 (median) of their local baseline versus 1.218 before; listed months sit at 0.42 of baseline shipped and 1.00 requested (operational rows).

In series with an ordering cycle the catch-up lands in an off-cycle month and looks like a small extra order. Examples: BSS-017 / Latin America (quarterly): 2019-07 shipped 16 of 73 requested, 2019-08 shows 22 = Backordered; BSS-044 / Asia Pacific: 2021-12 shipped 32 of 154, 2022-01 shows 48 = Backordered; BSS-057 / Latin America: 2023-11 shipped 237 of 375, 2023-12 shows 55. Of 248 positive values found in 37,691 off-cycle cells, 136 are exactly the previous listed month's back-order and 41 are listed months shipping part of a carry.

Semiconductor rows never back-order, so the ELA shortage produces a dip with no rebound.

**(b) Classification:** generator_structure / real_event. **(c) Confidence:** high.

**(d) Rule.** Unconstrained demand: month t listed -> `Requested_Units`; month t+1 unlisted with `Units_Sold(t+1) >= Backordered(t)` -> `Units_Sold(t+1) - Backordered(t)`. Run this before ordering-cycle detection and intermittency classification, otherwise 141+ phantom orders break strict cycles. Anomaly register: type "stockout" (action: replace by Requested) and type "back-order catch-up" (action: subtract carried-in units).

## 5. Semiconductor shortage: every ELA series-month from 2021-03 to 2022-09 is constrained; 31% of them are not listed

**(a) Evidence**

- All 4,314 "Semiconductor allocation" rows are Electrical Assemblies, 2021-03 .. 2022-09, exactly the window of events_calendar EV-019. No operational reason is ever listed for an ELA cell inside the window.
- ELA cells in the window with a train row: 6,221. Listed: 4,296 (69.06%), plus 18 listed cells whose train row is missing. Unlisted: 1,925 (plus 7 cells with neither a train row nor a listing).
- Listing is an independent coin flip per cell: share by month 65.8% .. 74.5%; by region 67.4% .. 70.2%; zero-demand cells 70.6% vs positive 68.8%; by severity quartile 67.6% .. 70.7%; binomial dispersion ratio across series 0.96; P(listed | previous listed) 69.3% vs 68.7% otherwise.
- Unlisted cells are constrained just as hard: within 320 series, unlisted `Units_Sold` / listed `Requested` = 0.662, listed `Shipped` / `Requested` = 0.664 (it would be about 1.0 if unlisted months were unconstrained).
- Nothing is constrained outside the window: the ELA-vs-other-families shipment index (continuing series, base 2020-07..2021-02) is 1.16 in 2021-02, 1.03 in 2021-03 (depth 0.09), 1.13 in 2022-09 (depth 0.08) and 1.15 in 2022-10.
- Fill follows `shortfall fraction = depth(month) x severity(series) + noise`:

| Month | 2021-03 | 04 | 05 | 06 | 07 | 08 | 09 | 10 | 11 | 12 | 2022-01 | 02 | 03 | 04 | 05 | 06 | 07 | 08 | 09 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| depth | .090 | .158 | .219 | .274 | .351 | .434 | .511 | .493 | .476 | .462 | .445 | .430 | .416 | .357 | .293 | .233 | .176 | .129 | .081 |
| mean listed fill % | 90.8 | 84.2 | 77.6 | 72.3 | 64.6 | 56.2 | 48.8 | 50.7 | 51.9 | 53.0 | 55.7 | 56.2 | 58.3 | 64.2 | 70.7 | 76.7 | 82.2 | 87.2 | 91.8 |

  Piecewise linear: about +0.07 per month for 6 months, about -0.016 per month for 6 months, about -0.058 per month for 6 months. Severity is one number per series (373 series, mean 1.00, sd 0.21, 5%-95% range 0.67 .. 1.33, consistent with Uniform(0.65, 1.35)); it is unrelated to region, customer, channel, powertrain or size class (group means 0.94 .. 1.06) and mostly not shared within a SKU. Residual noise is additive, sd 0.038, constant across months, lag-1 autocorrelation -0.09.
- Imputation test by hiding each listed month in turn (leave-one-out severity), 4,308 rows:

| Estimate of Requested | Bias | WAPE | MAPE (Requested > 0) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shipped, no correction | -33.8% | 33.8% | 34.8% |
| `u / (1 - depth)` (month only) | -3.1% | 11.0% | 12.1% |
| `(u + 0.5) / fill_hat`, per-series severity | -0.2% | 5.3% | 6.6% |
| same, rounded to integer | -0.2% | 5.3% | 6.3% |

  The `+0.5` removes the floor bias. On the real unlisted cells the imputed demand averages 0.989 of the same series' listed Requested (bootstrap 95% CI 0.931 .. 1.047).
- Size: inside the window ELA shipped 155,945 units against 234,232 demanded (ratio 0.666; 0.477 at the trough, 2021-09). ELA annual uplift of demand over shipments: 2021 +44.8% (150,251 vs 103,772), 2022 +29.2% (142,014 vs 109,950), other years +0.2% .. +0.4%.

**(b) Classification:** real_event (shortage) + generator_structure (listing coin flip, depth x severity). **(c) Confidence:** high that all window cells are constrained and on the depth curve; medium on the exact severity distribution.

**(d) Rule.** For every ELA cell with a train row in 2021-03 .. 2022-09: listed -> `Requested_Units`; unlisted -> `demand = max(0, round((Units_Sold + 0.5) / fill_hat) - carried_in)` if `Units_Sold > 0`, else 0, with `fill_hat = clip(1 - depth(month) x severity(series), 0.15, 0.98)`, `severity = sum(sf x depth) / sum(depth^2)` over that series' listed months (`sf = 1 - Fill_Rate_Pct/100`), and severity = 1.0 when fewer than 2 months are listed. Tables: `semi_depth_by_month.csv`, `semi_severity_by_series.csv`. Anomaly register: one event "EV-019 semiconductor allocation" covering all 6,239 ELA cells, flag `listed` / `imputed`, action "replace by unconstrained demand". Give imputed cells a sample weight of about 0.7.

## 6. Operational stockouts: random, about 79% listed; what can and cannot be recovered

**(a) Evidence**

*Process.* 1,516 listed operational rows; 1,508 on cells with a train row out of 238,344 non-shortage cells = 6.33 per 1,000 series-months. The rate is flat across every dimension tested:

| Dimension | Range of listed rate per 1,000 cells |
|---|---|
| Year 2019 .. 2026 | 5.4 .. 7.2 (linear trend +0.003 per month, nil) |
| Family | 5.5 (BSS) .. 7.1 (THM) |
| Region | 6.0 .. 7.1 |
| Channel | 5.8 .. 7.0 |
| Calendar month | 5.8 .. 7.1 |
| Volume quintile | 5.8 .. 7.4 |

Requested / series median is 1.08-1.12 for every reason versus 1.07 for all normal months, so stockouts do not select high-demand months. Cross-region coincidences for one SKU-month: 22 pairs observed, 19.3 expected under independence. Reasons are equiprobable and redrawn each month (same reason in consecutive listed months 26%). 22.9% of listed first months have a listed second month; runs longer than 2 months essentially do not occur (4 runs of 3 and one of 7 in about 1,230 runs). Implied generator: start probability about 0.6% per series-month, 30% chance of a second month, fill Uniform(15, 70) redrawn each month, 40% of the shortfall back-ordered.

*How incomplete.* Two independent estimates of the listing probability:

| Method | Listed | Hidden | Listing probability (Wilson 95% CI) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Listed rows with `Carried_In > 0`: is the previous month (which must have been a stockout) listed? | 251 | 64 | 0.797 (0.749 .. 0.838) |
| Phantom orders in off-cycle months of period-2 and period-3 series: is the previous month listed? | 106 | 33 | 0.763 (0.685 .. 0.826) |
| Pooled | 357 | 97 | 0.786 (0.746 .. 0.822) |

Hidden operational stockout months = 1,516 x (1 - 0.786) / 0.786 = about 413 (328 .. 516). This listing rate differs from the semiconductor rate (0.691 +/- 0.006).

*Exact detectors (no statistics involved).*

| Detector | Signature | Found | What it gives |
|---|---|---|---|
| D2 | listed row has `Carried_In > 0` but month t-1 is unlisted | 64 (62 with a usable train value) | month t-1 was a stockout with `Backordered = Carried_In(t)`; shortfall S in [ceil(2.5 x c), ceil(2.5 x (c+1)) - 1]; `demand(t-1) = Units_Sold(t-1) + S`, error at most 1 unit. Implied fill of these months: mean 0.40, range 0.14 .. 0.68, i.e. the Uniform(15, 70) law |
| D1 | positive units in an off-cycle month of a period-2 or period-3 ordering cycle, previous month unlisted and on-cycle, implied fill in [0.13, 0.72], implied demand within 0.25 .. 2.2 of the local baseline | 33 candidates pass (4 fail); 29 applied after overlap checks | previous month was a stockout; `demand(t-1) = Units_Sold(t-1) + S(u_t)`; the phantom month's demand is 0 |
| D3 | listed month with back-order, next month unlisted and `Units_Sold(t+1) < Backordered(t)` | 14 | month t+1 is a hidden second-month stockout; demand 0 if off-cycle, else unknown |

Examples. D2: BSS-024 / North America, 2020-05 shipped 5 (baseline 73), 2020-06 listed with Carried_In 12 -> hidden shortfall 30-32, demand 35-37. D1: BSS-071 / India, 2024-05 shipped 27 and the off-cycle 2024-06 shows 20 -> demand 77-79 (neighbouring orders 88, 61, 105). D3: CSS-066 / Europe, 2025-11 listed (Backordered 10), 2025-12 (off-cycle) shows 1.

*Measured by hiding listed months.* D1 flags 139 of 1,332 listed operational months with a shortfall (recall 10.4% of months, 17.8% of shortfall units); it can only fire when the following month is off-cycle (11.0% of cases). Its plausibility filter keeps 106 of 111 true phantom orders (95.5%). The 33 prev-unlisted detections compare with about 30 expected from the listing rate, so precision is about 90% or better. Together D1 + D2 + D3 recover 105 of the about 413 hidden months (about 25%).

*Statistical detector for monthly-ordering series (D4).* Likelihood ratio of "fill ~ U(0.15, 0.70), then rebound of 0.4 x shortfall" against "ordinary noise" using a local-median baseline, a region-month common factor and a per-series log-noise scale (median 0.35). Evaluated on 566 hidden listed positives against 158,329 unlisted cells:

| Recall | Cells flagged | Precision vs listed | Precision adjusted for hidden true stockouts |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5% | 53 | 54.7% | 69.6% |
| 10% | 126 | 45.2% | 57.6% |
| 20% | 373 | 30.6% | 38.9% |
| 30% | 681 | 25.0% | 31.8% |
| 50% | 2,307 | 12.3% | 15.6% |
| 70% | 8,196 | 4.8% | 6.2% |

AUC 0.934 (dip-only 0.927, naive lowest-ratio 0.924). The limit is the demand noise itself: 6.0% of ordinary months are below half of their baseline and 18.7% below 0.7, against a 0.36% base rate; cross-series factors (SKU, family, customer, channel by month) explain about 1% of the residual variance, so no better baseline exists. No side channel either: listed rows have the same load lag (31.63 days) and the same share of multi-version Record_IDs (1.6% vs 1.5%) as other rows.

**(b) Classification:** real_event (random operational stockouts) + generator_structure (listing rate). **(c) Confidence:** high for process and exact detectors; medium for the hidden count.

**(d) Rule.** Apply D2, D1, D3 as exact corrections (`hidden_stockouts_detected_register.csv`, 134 rows including the 29 phantom months). Do not impute from D4: write its top cells (LR >= 50, 82 cells, `d4_suspected_unlisted_stockouts.csv`) to the anomaly register as "suspected unlisted stockout, about 60% confidence, no action". The remaining about 310 hidden months are 0.13% of cells and about 5.4k units out of 11.8M; handle them with a robust loss, not with a detector. Do not build stockout features for the forecast: the process has no predictable structure and rule 7 says the forecast window has no supply limits.

## 8. Supply-type calendar events that are NOT in the stockout file

**(a) Evidence**

- **Red Sea disruption (EV-039, Export channel, 2024-01 .. 2024-03).** 276 Export series in Europe (48) and Middle East & Africa (228). On the 156 with strictly monthly orders, median `Units_Sold` / own baseline is 0.58 in 2024-01, 0.71 in 2024-02 and 1.43 in 2024-03 (means 0.60, 0.74, 1.52), against 0.94, 1.07, 1.02 for non-export series in the same regions and 0.88, 0.91, 1.06 for Export series elsewhere. January to March together is 0.95 of three normal months. The stockout file has no matching rows: 11 listed rows on 817 cells (5.9 expected), only 2 of the 13 Export rows in the window carry "Logistics delay". The mechanism is not the back-order mechanism: quarterly Export series show no phantom units in off-cycle February or March (CSS-011 / Europe: 205, 0, 0, 228), while the 7 bi-monthly series inspected by eye that order in February look depressed in February and elevated in April (not quantified).
- **Latin America ERP migration (EV-033, 2023-03 .. 2023-05).** Units and revenue are blank for essentially all non-zero cells of the Aftermarket and Export channels in Latin America in those three months: 145, 147 and 146 Latin America cells have no units versus 30-41 in neighbouring months (about 110 extra per month); Aftermarket totals are 0, 0, 0 units and Export totals 0, 65, 0, the 65 being the one cell restored from the stockout file. This is missing data, not zero demand and not a stockout; one cell is recoverable from the stockout file.
- **COVID lockdowns (EV-009 .. EV-013).** Demand-side: 63.5% of ordinary cells are below half of their baseline in 2020-04 and 53.6% in 2020-05; operational stockout listings are not elevated in 2020 (6.4 per 1,000).

**(b) Classification:** real_event (Red Sea, COVID); data_error (ERP blanks). **(c) Confidence:** high that they exist and are outside the stockout mechanism; medium on the Red Sea multipliers; low on its exact rule.

**(d) Rule.** Red Sea: event flag on Export x {Europe, MEA} x 2024-01..03 (plus 2024-04 for series with no March order); either mask those months in training or model them with event dummies; the events lens should settle whether to redistribute units. ERP months: set to missing and impute, never zero. None of these belong in the lost-sales totals of Finding 7.

## 9. Exact algorithm for the unconstrained-demand series and what the forecaster trains on

Reference implementation: `p40_build_unconstrained.py`; output `unconstrained_demand.parquet` (289,802 rows = 3,083 series x 94 months; columns `units_shipped_clean`, `demand_uc`, `uc_source`, `fill_used`, `shortfall_est`, `lost_est`, `bo_to_next`, `carry_removed`, `price`, `lost_rev`, `off`, `offP`, `semi_cell`).

Order of operations on the cleaned one-row-per-Date-SKU-Region panel:

0. Overlay `Units_Sold := Shipped_Units` on listed cells (Finding 3).
1. **S1, listed month (5,830 cells):** `demand = Requested_Units`.
2. **S5, unlisted ELA cell in 2021-03 .. 2022-09 (1,925 cells):** `demand = max(0, round((u + 0.5) / fill_hat) - Backordered(t-1 if listed))`, 0 if `u = 0`.
3. **S2, unlisted month after a listed month with back-order, `u >= Backordered(t-1)` (1,034 cells):** `demand = u - Backordered(t-1)`.
4. **D3, same but `u < Backordered(t-1)` (14 cells):** demand 0 if the month is off-cycle, otherwise missing.
5. **D2 (62 cells):** unlisted month followed by a listed month with `Carried_In = c > 0`: `demand = u + (ceil(2.5c) + ceil(2.5(c+1)) - 1) / 2`.
6. **D1 (29 + 29 cells):** phantom order `u_t > 0` in an off-cycle month (period 2 or 3: all of `t +/- P, +/- 2P, +/- 3P` (and `+/- 12` for P = 3) that exist are zero, at least 3 of them; or at most one positive when at least 5 are zero), previous month unlisted, on-cycle, implied fill `u_{t-1} / (u_{t-1} + S)` in [0.13, 0.72], `(u_{t-1} + S) / baseline` in [0.25, 2.2] with `S = (ceil(2.5 u_t) + ceil(2.5 (u_t + 1)) - 1) / 2`: `demand(t-1) = u_{t-1} + S`, `demand(t) = 0`.
7. Everything else: `demand = Units_Sold` (missing stays missing).

Source counts: as shipped 235,337; missing 45,542; S1 5,830; S5 1,925; S2 1,034; D2 62; D1 29 + 29; D3 14.

**Train on `demand_uc`, not on `Units_Sold`.** Compute lags, rolling statistics, intermittency class, ordering-cycle detection and backtest actuals from `demand_uc`. Mask the D3 on-cycle cells. Weight S5 cells about 0.7. Do not add the 178 units back-ordered out of 2026-10 (16 series) to the 2026-11 forecast: rule 7 asks for requested demand. The effect on the forecast origin is small for most series (last-6-month uplift of unconstrained over shipped is +0.24% in aggregate; 124 listed rows in 2026-05..10 with 5,728 requested vs 2,447 shipped), but large for individual series such as ELA-008 / India (2026-10: shipped 76, requested 167) and CSS-006 / Europe (74 vs 157).

**(b) Classification:** generator_structure. **(c) Confidence:** high.

## Open questions, ranked by likely impact on forecast accuracy

1. **Is ELA demand during the shortage "inflated"?** For 227 continuing ELA series, unconstrained ELA demand relative to other families runs at 1.08 .. 1.36 (mean 1.19) of its 2019 + 2023 norm inside the window, against 1.08-1.10 in the two months before and 1.05-1.09 in the four months after. ELA also fell further in COVID (0.76 .. 0.79 in 2020-06..08), so a higher macro beta may explain it; if instead the generator adds over-ordering under allocation, a driver model fitted on the window will overstate ELA's sensitivity. The macro lens should test this; until then consider down-weighting ELA window months in driver regressions.
2. **Is the hidden test target pure requested demand?** Rule 7 says so. If the organisers' truth were shipments, 2026-11 would also contain the 178 units back-ordered from 2026-10.
3. **Red Sea rule.** Multipliers of about 0.6 / 0.7 / 1.45 on Export x Europe/MEA are clear, but the exact mechanism for cyclic series (catch-up in April?) is not established, so the unconstrained series does not correct these months.
4. **Why two listing rates (0.69 semiconductor vs 0.79 operational)?** Statistically distinct (pooled operational CI 0.746 .. 0.822). It only changes the hidden-month estimate (413; 650 if 0.70 applied).
5. **Undetected hidden operational stockouts (about 310 months).** Not identifiable at useful precision; about 5.4k units. Robust loss is the mitigation.
6. **Official clean vs my working clean.** The 343 unlisted India pack-of-10 cells (+/-5 units each) and the 331 blank ERP cells need the official treatment before the unconstrained series is final.
